items.title: Sandia demonstrates continual-learning improvements in AIGM Lite
items.summary: Sandia's three-year AIGM Lite LDRD project has completed core components of a fast-and-slow continual-learning architecture for sensor-data models. Controlled incremental-learning tests reported accuracy above 90 percent versus above 70 percent for the baseline, with novelty detection, human-reviewed updates and unsupervised clustering now being integrated. The official source does not establish Genesis Mission affiliation.
items.evidence_note: Sandia identifies AIGM Lite as an internally funded Laboratory Directed Research and Development project. No official Genesis Mission or verified Genesis-project connection was found.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Systems Biology Modeling campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites teams to combine multiomics data, metabolic modeling and SI analysis. Reusable workflows will help explain microbial pathways and support biotechnology and critical-material recovery. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Quantum Computing for Metallophores campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites researchers to benchmark hybrid classical-quantum methods for microbial metal-binding molecules. Shared reference datasets and validated workflows could support critical-mineral recovery research. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 NextGen Molecular Workflows campaign
items.summary: EMSL is connecting CoreMS molecular annotation and SIMPLE simulations through SI agents. The campaign will produce interoperable datasets and validated workflows for biodesign and critical-mineral research. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: EMSL opens FY 2027 Assured SI for Autonomous Biology campaign
items.summary: EMSL invites research teams to evaluate autonomous biological workflows and develop shared reliability diagnostics and reporting standards. This addresses trust and reproducibility in AI-directed experiments. Proposals due December 1, 2026; work begins December 15. No confirmed Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: Argonne expands ALCF Inference Service with Tara and Minerva
items.summary: New Tara and Minerva systems expand shared model-serving capacity for Genesis Mission teams and the broader ALCF research community. The service offers more than 50 models and is developing support for agent-assisted scientific workflows.

items.title: DOE Secretary visits University of Oklahoma's two Genesis Mission research teams
items.summary: University of Oklahoma reports that Energy Secretary Chris Wright met with Genesis researchers Oct. 30. Two OU-led teams received nearly $1.4 million in Phase I funding, including Ahmad Ghassemi's machine-learning and physics-based geothermal work and Grant Biedermann's quantum research.
items.evidence_note: University primary-source reporting of DOE Genesis research; linked to existing OU projects.

items.title: Aclara and Argonne validate rare-earth separation model; Genesis digital twin planned
items.summary: Aclara reports that its Argonne CRADA delivered a validated steady-state rare-earth separation model for Project Dynamo. Aclara, Argonne and Virginia Tech were selected for Genesis Phase I to pursue an AI-supported dynamic digital twin; the DOE award agreement was still being finalized on Nov. 2.
items.evidence_note: Company reports DOE Genesis Phase I selection; separate completed CRADA from prospective DOE award and planned dynamic twin.

items.title: Cadence joins Genesis Mission Consortium for AI-driven science and microelectronics
items.summary: Cadence announced Oct. 29 that it joined the Genesis Mission Consortium and plans to contribute AI-enabled electronic design automation, simulation and digital-twin expertise to DOE laboratory collaborations. Consortium participation is confirmed, but no specific project award is claimed.
items.evidence_note: Cadence press release and Genesis Mission Consortium news list confirm membership only; no specific Genesis grant asserted.

items.title: PNNL launches BattMan Accelerator for SI-driven battery manufacturing
items.summary: The Battery Manufacturing Accelerator brings laboratories and universities together to advance battery scale-up using SI, manufacturing data and digital tools. Industry partnerships are being formed. The announcement does not establish Genesis Mission affiliation.

items.title: DOE, NIH and Biohub partner on Genesis-aligned predictive biology data
items.summary: DOE Office of Science, NIH and Biohub signed an MOU to develop SI-ready biological datasets and predictive models of living systems. DOE explicitly says the partnership delivers on the national Genesis Mission; NIH identifies Bio Genesis as its contribution to that mission. This is an interagency partnership, not a new award to a specific DOE Genesis project.
items.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science
items.evidence_note: DOE states partnership delivers on Genesis Mission EO; NIH states Bio Genesis is NIH contribution to national Genesis Mission. Do not equate Bio Genesis program with a specific DOE-funded project.
